Deep learning-based segmentation of the ischemic core and severe hypodensity on noncontrast head CT compared with CT perfusion and diffusion-weighted imaging.
desc: [European radiology] To compare the spatial overlap, imaging marker agreement, and outcome associations of acute ischemic regions of interest (ROIs) using deep-learning NCCT (DLNCCT) versus manual NCCT, CTP, and DWI-based segmentations. We trained a deep learning model to segment ischemic ROIs on admission NCCT (DLNCCT). DLNCCT was compared with manual NCCT, CTP (rCBF < 30%/38%), and DWI using the Dice similarity coefficient (mean ± SD), Bland-Altman analysis (mean difference [95% CI]), and concordance correlation coefficient (CCC). For each ROI, we compared NCCT imaging biomarkers: average lesion density (HU); modified net water uptake (mNWU in %); total volume (mL); and hypodense (≤ 26 HU) volume (mL). DLNCCT biomarkers were associated with reversed 90-day ordinal modified Rankin Scale (genOR [95% CI]). We used 218/762 train/test cases. Dice was 0.30 ± 0.30 between DLNCCT and manual segmentation, 0.22 ± 0.25 between DLNCCT-DWI, and 0.15 ± 0.22/0.21 ± 0.24 between CTP (rCBF < 30%/< 38%)-DWI. DLNCCT-DWI biomarker agreement was -1 HU (95% CI: -7; 6) for average density (CCC: 0.71), 4.9% (95% CI: -7.0; 16.8) for mNWU (CCC: 0.35), -16 mL (95% CI: -108; 76) for total volume (CCC: 0.57), and -4 mL (95% CI: -31; 23) for hypodense lesion volume (CCC: 0.75). Average lesion density (1.11 [95% CI: 1.06; 1.16]) and hypodense volume (0.85 [95% CI: 0.72; 0.99]) were associated with 90-day mRS. Spatial and biomarker agreement between DLNCCT and DWI was suboptimal but comparable to CTP-DWI. Nevertheless, DLNCCT-derived average lesion density and hypodense volume were associated with functional outcomes. Question Deep-learning models segment ischemic tissue on NCCT, but their spatial overlap and accuracy of imaging biomarker assessment relative to DWI and CTP core remain unclear. Findings Deep-learning NCCT segmentation showed good agreement with DWI in measuring hypodense (≤ 26 HU) volumes (- 4 mL [95% CI: -31; 23]; CCC 0.75). Clinical relevance Despite limited spatial overlap, NCCT-derived deep learning biomarkers showed agreement comparable to DWI, with improved performance in patients with poor ASPECTS and collateral scores. Hypodense volume and average lesion density were associated with functional outcome.

title: MotionBench-XAI: Benchmarking What Shapes Shapley Explanations in Spatiotemporal Machine Learning
desc: Predicting outcomes from spatiotemporal data, such as assessing Parkinson's severity from human motion, often requires explainability in addition to accuracy. Practitioners need to know what drove the prediction, whether it be spatial (a body joint), temporal (a specific window), or both. Shapley values are attributions computed by treating input features as players in a cooperative game and measuring how the model output changes as coalitions of players are removed. Computing them involves choosing what counts as players, how absent players are imputed, and how the game is evaluated. How these choices affect explanation quality is poorly understood for spatiotemporal data, and real data carries no ground-truth attributions to check against. We present MotionBench-XAI, a benchmark built on i) five synthetic spatiotemporal datasets with exact ground-truth Shapley values, ii) three real datasets across clinical gait, electrocardiogram, and audio, iii) ten attribution methods across three player sets, and iv) three trained architectures. We show that grouping features into players, across time, space, or both, matters more than the choice of imputer. Generative imputers improve explanations only when their conditional models are accurate. On real data, the standard proxy metrics select contradictory best methods. We distill these findings into practical insights and provide an open-source pipeline.

title: Quantum computing may still be a decade away
Nurses' Attitudes and Experiences With Generative AI in Clinical Practice: Qualitative Systematic Review.
source: PubMed · Journal of medical Internet research
desc: [Journal of medical Internet research] The rapid advancement of generative AI (GenAI) holds transformative potential for clinical nursing practice, yet its integration also brings significant risks and uncertainties. Despite growing discourse on AI in health care, frontline nurses' firsthand experiences, perceptions, and practical needs regarding GenAI remain largely under-synthesized in the existing literature. This systematic review aimed to synthesize qualitative evidence to clarify the core themes related to clinical nurses' perceptions, experiences, obstacles, and requirements when using GenAI in real-world clinical settings. A systematic search was conducted across 10 electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, ProQuest Dissertations and Theses, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, VIP Information, SinoMed, and Wanfang) for records published between January 2018 and June 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative and mixed methods studies involving registered nurses that explored their perceptions and experiences of GenAI in clinical practice. Two independent reviewers (MMW and CYZ) performed study selection, quality appraisal, and data extraction, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Qualitative Research. Extracted data encompassed study characteristics, participant demographics, and GenAI-related contextual factors. Data synthesis followed Thomas and Harden's 3-phase thematic synthesis: initial inductive coding generated descriptive themes, which were subsequently integrated with the Technology Acceptance Model for Artificial Intelligence in Nursing (TAM-AIN) framework to develop higher-order analytical themes. Certainty in the evidence was evaluated using the GRADE-CERQual (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation-Confidence in the Evidence from Reviews of Qualitative Research). Of the 4350 initially identified records, 13 studies from 6 countries (China: n=6; Saudi Arabia: n=3; United States, Singapore, Australia, and South Korea: n=1 each) met the inclusion criteria, encompassing qualitative data from 234 registered nurses. Three main themes emerged: patterns of nurses' engagement with GenAI (ranging from passive observation to proactive integration), multidimensional perceived threats to adoption (functional, professional, and accountability-related), and the moderating role of organizational readiness, which influenced

title: GenStrain: Multi-Conditional Generative Diffusion Model To Synthesize High-quality Motion and Strain Maps From Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Images
desc: This paper presents GenStrain, a novel method for synthesizing high-quality cardiac motion-based strain maps from routinely collected cine cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) images. Existing approaches typically rely on image registration to estimate motion (a sequence of displacements) from cine CMR images, but cine CMR presents very sparse trackable intramyocardial features, presenting challenges to estimate intramyocardial motion. An advanced imaging technique, Displacement Encoding with Stimulated Echoes (DENSE) CMR, is considered as the gold standard for strain assessment, but it requires additional acquisitions, which are not ideal for efficient clinical workflows. To address this gap, we introduce GenStrain, a novel framework designed to learn the data distribution of highly accurate cardiac motion captured by DENSE. In particular, we develop a diffusion process in motion space, where spatiotemporal continuity is carefully considered. To fully leverage both cine CMR images and their associated motion patterns, we introduce a multi-conditional conditioning strategy that integrates anatomical features and motion representations learned by a spatiotemporal registration model to guide the generation process. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed model, GenStrain, outperforms existing strain analysis methods based on displacement estimates from both traditional registration approaches and state-of-the-art (SOTA) deep learning models. Our model represents a promising step toward more accurate cardiac function assessment and holds great potential for clinical translation. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Rishov-MIA/GenStrain.

title: Ngai Yeung
Multimodal imaging and artificial intelligence for bone tumor diagnosis: Comparative performance and emerging technologies.
desc: [Journal of bone oncology] Multimodal imaging is central to the diagnosis, staging, and management of bone tumors. Radiography and computed tomography remain essential for initial assessment and cortical evaluation, magnetic resonance imaging provides superior soft tissue contrast and local staging accuracy, and positron emission tomography enhances detection of metastatic disease and treatment response. No single technique suffices across clinical scenarios. Advances in artificial intelligence and radiomics offer avenues to augment this framework, with demonstrated potential in lesion classification, segmentation, prognostication, and response prediction. This review advances a specific argument rather than surveying available technologies: that the principal constraint on artificial intelligence in musculoskeletal oncology is the stability of the reference standard rather than algorithmic capability. Ground truth in bone tumors is unstable on four grounds. Core needle biopsy samples a limited volume and may miss the highest-grade component: agreement between biopsy and resection grade in central chondrosarcoma falls from a weighted kappa of 0.63 in long bones to 0.12 in the pelvis. Expert interpretation is itself inconsistent, with interobserver kappa for grading cartilaginous tumors of 0.44 among musculoskeletal pathologists and 0.35 among radiologists. Molecular criteria have redefined entities within the past decade, so older datasets contain classes that no longer exist as defined. And histological classification does not reliably predict clinical behavior. Consequently, measurable accuracy has a ceiling set by the reference standard rather than the algorithm, and apparent failure on external validation may reflect label divergence between institutions rather than model deficiency. Evidence is graded throughout, and clinical readiness distinguished from technical performance. No system for primary bone tumor characterization has regulatory clearance in the United States or Europe, and formal appraisal of this literature confirms low methodological compliance and infrequent external validation. Progress will depend on multicenter validation and protocol harmonization, and, distinctively for this field, on composite reference standards, outcome-based endpoints, and explicit uncertainty modelling, since ground-truth instability can be mitigated but not eliminated.

title: RapidMitDet: Boosting Computational Efficiency for Mitosis Detection via Magnification Alignment
desc: Automated mitosis detection is a critical research focus, enabling pathologists to rapidly assess mitotic indices for tumor malignancy evaluation. However, most of the existing detection approaches suffer from significant computational inefficiency due to the giga-pixel image resolution of Whole-Slide Images (WSIs), which greatly hinders their clinical applicability. In this study, we propose RapidMitDet, a computational efficient mitosis detection approach. Our method employs a coarse-to-fine framework, first identifying mitotic candidates at lower magnification and then confirming them at higher magnification. In the coarse-detection stage, we introduce magnification-aligned knowledge distillation to reduce the information gap between magnification levels while minimizing the performance degradation in the lower magnification detection model. In the subsequent fine-classification stage, we propose adaptive triplet learning (ATL) to optimize infomative sample selection, thereby enhancing discrimination between mitotic and non-mitotic instances. Experimental results show that RapidMitDet achieves the optimal accuracy-efficiency balance at 20x magnification, improving computational speed by up to 5.62 times over the latest state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. Due to its lightweight model design, RapidMitDet can also deliver efficient detection at higher magnification (40x) while achieving even higher detection performance. In WSI-level evaluations, our method shows strong agreement with pathologists' diagnoses (ICCs: 0.879 (40x), 0.822 (20x)) while maintaining superior efficiency, highlighting its potential for clinical application. Code is available at https://github.com/logincat/RapidMitDet

title: People channel feed
Electrocardiogram-based artificial intelligence to predict incident heart failure with preserved versus reduced ejection fraction.
desc: [Journal of cardiac failure] Heart failure is classically divided into two subtypes based on the ejection fraction (EF): HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), each with varying risk mitigation strategies. Electrocardiogram-based artificial intelligence (AI) may facilitate HF subtype-specific risk prediction, to enable tailored prevention. Based on a previously validated HF prediction architecture, we developed an ECG-based AI model to predict 10-year risk of incident HFrEF (LVEF <50%) versus HFpEF (LVEF ≥50%) (Electrocardiogram to Heart Failure Subtype, "ECG2HF-Subtype"). ECG2HF-Subtype was developed in 98,190 individuals in Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH), and validated in three test sets: MGH, Brigham and Women's Hospital (BWH), and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC), among individuals without prior HF. HF was identified using a validated natural language processing model, and subtypes were classified by LVEF proximate to incident HF. Discrimination was quantified using time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and average precision (AP), with comparisons to age and sex, and a multinomial logistic regression classifier including PREVENT-HF variables. In aggregate, models were evaluated in MGH (n=16,739, age 56±17, 54% women), BWH (n=75,195, 56±16, 59%) and BIDMC (n=30,133, 56±17, 54%). ECG2HF-Subtype consistently discriminated incident HFrEF (MGH 10-year AUROC 0.89 [0.86-0.91], 10-year AP: 0.11 [95%CI 0.09-0.15], cumulative incidence 1.73%; BWH: 0.88 [0.87-0.89], 0.13 [0.11-0.14], 2.23% BIDMC: 0.88 [0.86-0.89], 0.14 [0.12-0.17], 2.19%) and HFpEF events (MGH 10-year AUROC 0.83 [0.81-0.85], 10-year AP: 0.10 [95% CI 0.09-0.13], cumulative incidence 3.17%; BWH: 0.79 [0.77-0.80], 0.06 [0.06-0.07], 2.75%), BIDMC: 0.81 [0.80-0.82], 0.10 [0.09-0.12], 3.49%), with consistently greater AUROC versus age and sex. When compared to PREVENT-HF variables, ECG2HF-Subtypes had favorable discrimination of HFrEF (e.g., 10-year AUROC in MGH+BWH 0.86 [0.84-0.88] vs. 0.78 [0.76-0.80]), and modestly lower for HFpEF (10-year AUROC in MGH+BWH 0.78 [0.76-0.80] vs. 0.81 [0.79-0.82]). By predicting risk of HFpEF and HFrEF, AI-enabled ECG analysis may enable targeted prevention to reduce HF-related morbidity.

title: Volumetric Latent Diffusion for Brain Tumour Segmentation with Missing Modalities
desc: Brain tumour segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging normally assumes that all four imaging sequences are available, but in clinical practice one or more are frequently missing. Existing methods for incomplete inputs learn modality-invariant representations or distil from a full-modality teacher, and return a single deterministic mask. Gen- erative formulations instead model a distribution over plausible masks, but the cost of sampling at full resolution has largely confined them to two dimensions. This paper proposes a three-dimensional conditional latent diffusion framework for whole-tumour segmentation from incom- plete multi-sequence MRI. Images and annotations are first compressed by two volumetric autoencoders, which makes diffusion over whole vol- umes affordable, and sequences are dropped at random during training so that a single model handles every combination of missing sequences. Because the model samples rather than predicts, repeated draws also yield a voxel-wise map of disagreement at no extra training cost. Evalu- ations on 2,601 studies from BraTS 2023 and 2024 show that the method reaches 0.955 Dice with all four sequences and 0.904 with FLAIR alone, and that it is the most accurate of the four methods compared in eight of the fifteen configurations. The disagreement between draws widens as sequences are withheld, giving a signal that accompanies the prediction rather than replacing it

title: Artificial intelligence in esophageal cancer radiotherapy: a literature review.
desc: [Journal of thoracic disease] Radiotherapy is a key component in the management of esophageal cancer (EC). Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative tool for optimizing radiotherapy workflows. Numerous AI-based tools are being developed to improve efficiency and facilitate the personalization of radiation oncology. This study aimed to provide an up-to-date review of the literature on recent advances in AI applications across the EC radiotherapy workflow. The PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases were searched to retrieve original English-language articles published from January 1, 2020 to May 26, 2026. The following search terms were used: "Esophageal neoplasms", "esophageal cancer", "oesophageal cancer" AND "artificial intelligence", "AI" AND "radiation oncology", "radiotherapy", "radiation", "chemoradiotherapy". The included studies covered different steps in the radiotherapy workflow; that is, initial treatment decision-making, treatment planning and preparation, treatment delivery, and post-treatment follow-up. A total of 105 studies covering the different stages of the radiotherapy workflow were included in the review. Most studies focused on initial treatment decision-making, primarily benefit-risk stratification through predictive modeling of treatment outcomes and treatment-related toxicities, followed by treatment planning and preparation, particularly automated segmentation and treatment planning. Conversely, few studies investigated AI applications in treatment plan approval and quality assurance, or treatment delivery. Notably, most of the included studies were retrospective, with substantial heterogeneity in study designs, methodologies, and reporting. AI demonstrates substantial potential to facilitate clinical decision-making while improving the efficiency and accuracy of radiotherapy workflows. Future research should prioritize multicenter prospective studies, standardized methodological and reporting frameworks, and explainable AI (XAI) to improve the reliability, transparency, and clinical translation of AI models.

title: SideAge-RiskNet: Predicted Mammographic-Age Features for Future Breast Cancer Risk and Laterality Prediction
desc: Whether breast-specific mammographic aging provides information beyond chronological age for future cancer prediction remains unclear. We propose SideAge-RiskNet, a framework integrating predicted mammographic-age features with breast-specific representations for multi-year breast cancer risk and conditional laterality prediction. A side-aware DenseNet121 trained on never-cancer reference examinations estimates left and right breast ages. Age-adjusted residuals and bilateral age descriptors are subsequently fused with corresponding image representations, while clinical variables contribute through an image--clinical risk branch. The framework jointly predicts cumulative cancer risk over 1--5 years and the subsequently affected breast among unilateral cancer cases. Across 4,480 EMBED and 248 external examinations, pre-cancer scans demonstrated pronounced bilateral age asymmetry. SideAge-RiskNet established state-of-the-art performance in 1--5-year risk assessment over Mirai and AsymMirai with mean risk AUROCs of 81.73% on EMBED and 72.83% on CSMC. Furthermore, it enabled conditional cancer laterality prediction, achieving AUROCs of 73.26% and 82.53%, respectively. This demonstrates the critical utility of bilateral aging phenotypes in localized breast cancer risk surveillance.

title: Metabolic reprogramming of myeloid‑derived suppressor cells in colorectal cancer: Mechanistic insights and immunometabolic targeted rehabilitation (Review).
desc: [Molecular medicine reports] Metabolic reprogramming of myeloid‑derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) plays a role in immunotherapy resistance in colorectal cancer (CRC). This metabolic reprogramming appears to be coordinated by oncogenic mutations (such as adenomatous polyposis coli, KRAS and TP53) through a proposed self‑reinforcing 'mutation‑metabolism‑suppression' axis. In the present review, four core metabolic pillars sustaining MDSC pathogenicity and the epimetabolic regulation that durably locks them into a suppressive state were examined. Furthermore, two emerging dimensions were highlighted: The spatial metabolic antagonism through which MDSCs may construct a metabolically hostile zone to limit the functional activity of tertiary lymphoid structures, and the remote manipulation of MDSC function by gut and intratumoral microbiota‑derived metabolites. To transcend the limitations of non‑specific myeloid depletion, immunometabolic rehabilitation is proposed as a potentially transformative framework targeting intrinsic metabolic vulnerabilities to functionally reprogram MDSCs from an immunosuppressive to a homeostatic or immunostimulatory phenotype. By integrating emerging spatial omics for precise target validation, artificial intelligence‑guided rational drug design and microbiome modulation, this paradigm provides a strategic roadmap for next‑generation precision immunotherapy, aiming to achieve durable responses across both microsatellite stable and microsatellite instability‑high CRC.

title: Guardrail Erosion in Domain Fine-Tuned Large Language Models: A Paired Audit of Knowledge-Centric Abstention in Biomedical LLMs
desc: The number of domain fine-tuned models, particularly in the biomedical domain, is rapidly expanding. Fine-tuning promises high-performing models at a fraction of the cost of training a base model, but it can also produce unintended behavioral changes. Multiple studies have shown that safety guardrails can erode with fine-tuning, yet large-scale studies across model architectures, data mixtures, and fine-tuning methodologies remain limited. Where prior work in this space has studied value-centric refusal, this work focuses on knowledge-centric abstention. We audit 25 biomedical domain fine-tuned large language models against 11 paired base checkpoints on MedAbstain and ClinDet-Bench to evaluate the impact of fine-tuning on knowledge-centric abstention. We find that defined appropriate abstention measured by these benchmarks, already low in base models (median 8.3% on MedAbstain), falls further after fine-tuning (median 4.2%, decreasing in 21 of 25 pairs on MedAbstain), and that the magnitude and direction of change are heterogeneous across pairs. These results motivate fine-tuning methods that improve domain-specific capability while preserving appropriate caution.

title: Accuracy and reliability of privacy-compliant large language models for MRI protocol selection in radiological workflows.
desc: [European radiology] Accurate MRI protocolling is essential for diagnostic quality and workflow efficiency, yet manual protocol selection is time-consuming and variable. This study evaluated four contemporary open-weight large language models (LLMs) for MRI protocol and optional sequence selection from real-world clinical referrals. In this retrospective study, 1201 consecutive referral forms (mean age 58 ± 14 years; 646 men) were provided as unaltered text to each LLM, which selected an institutional protocol and optional sequences from predefined lists. A consensus of two board-certified radiologists served as reference. Performance was assessed at protocol and sequence levels using protocol accuracy and mean Jaccard index. Larger general-purpose models achieved the highest concordance with expert protocolling (GPT-OSS-120B: Jaccard 0.96, 95% CI: 0.96-0.97; accuracy 0.94, 0.93-0.95; Qwen-3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507: Jaccard 0.96, 0.95-0.97; accuracy 0.94, 0.93-0.96), outperforming MedGemma-27B-Text-IT (Jaccard 0.85, 0.84-0.87; accuracy 0.79, 0.76-0.81) and Gemma-3-27B-IT (Jaccard 0.61, 0.59-0.63; accuracy 0.58, 0.55-0.60). Unacceptable protocol selections ranged from 70/1201 cases (5.8%) for GPT-OSS and 71/1201 (5.9%) for Qwen3 to 297/1201 (24.7%) for MedGemma and 820/1,201 (68.3%) for Gemma3. Among unacceptable cases, the most common error was anatomically correct but clinically suboptimal protocol selection (57.7-70.7%), followed by incorrect anatomical region (11.6-39.4%) and optional-sequence-only errors (2.8-30.2%). GPT-OSS matched expert scan duration (p = 0.18), Qwen3 was shorter (p = 0.002), and Gemma3 and MedGemma were longer (both p < 0.001). Open-weight LLMs showed high concordance with expert MRI protocolling and may support standardized protocol selection. However, clinically relevant errors persisted, underscoring the need for radiologist oversight. Question Can open-weight LLMs support accurate and standardized MRI protocol and sequence selection from clinical referrals compared with expert reference standards? Findings In 1201 referrals, LLMs achieved high concordance with expert MRI protocol selection (accuracy up to 0.94; mean Jaccard index up to 0.96), but unacceptable errors remained model-dependent and ranged from 5.8% to 68.3%. Clinical relevance Open-weight LLMs showed high agreement with expert MRI protocol decisions from clinical text and may support standardized, reliable, and scalable MRI protocolling while maintaining radiologist oversight.

title: VoluCompose: Constructing Compact Volumetric Visual Representations for Medical Image Understanding
desc: Medical vision--language models can interpret volumetric images, but processing full volumes is costly because hundreds of slices produce long, redundant visual-token sequences. Existing compression methods often couple content selection with budget determination. We observe that neighboring slices share visual features and that attention concentration varies across visual encoders. We propose VoluCompose, a training-free, model-agnostic framework that separates what visual content to retain from how many tokens to allocate. Its hyperbolic token composition module groups contiguous slices into ordered support units and uses the Lorentz distance to account for feature magnitude and direction during token allocation, anchor selection, and refinement. Its capacity control module uses visual-encoder attention entropy to allocate more tokens when attention is more dispersed. We evaluate VoluCompose on two tasks across three datasets and four backbones. Across nine calibrated settings, VoluCompose attains the highest mean quality--retention hypervolume among the compared methods. It achieves a mean relative quality of 121.68\% against the uncompressed references while retaining 22.78% of visual tokens on average. Compression remains robust even at a 10% token budget. Across settings, the lowest ROUGE-L ratio to the uncompressed reference is 96.4\% for VoluCompose. The corresponding minima for the compression baselines range from 15.0% to 70.5%. Code is available at https://github.com/yezanting/VoluCompose.

title: Applications, Technical Characteristics, and Evaluation Approaches of Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Nursing: Scoping Review.
source: PubMed · Journal of medical Internet research
desc: [Journal of medical Internet research] Large language models (LLMs) show great potential for widespread application in the field of nursing; however, their limitations include hallucinations, insufficient domain knowledge, and delays in updating evidence. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), by combining external knowledge retrieval with text generation, holds promise for optimizing model outputs. However, current evidence on the use of RAG in nursing remains fragmented and has not been systematically synthesized. This scoping review aims to map the applications of RAG in the nursing field, identify current research characteristics and gaps, and provide a foundational evidence base to inform future research and development of intelligent tools for nursing practice. This study adopted the Arksey and O'Malley scoping review framework and followed PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) reporting standards. We systematically searched 9 databases-PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, CNKI, VIP Database, Wanfang Database, and Sinomed-from inception to September 2026. Backward and forward citation searches were also conducted to identify additional eligible studies. Eligible publications were restricted to those in English or Chinese during study selection. Two independent reviewers completed study screening and data extraction, and descriptive synthesis was performed for all eligible records. A total of 28 studies published between 2024 and 2026 were included. The application of RAG in nursing primarily focused on 4 scenarios: patient education (n=9), nursing informatics (n=8), clinical decision support (n=7), and nursing education (n=4). The base LLMs included the GPT series, LLaMA, ChatGLM, and Doubao, among others, while the knowledge bases primarily integrated literature, clinical guidelines, institutional resources, and clinical data. Most studies relied on dense retrieval, while some incorporated hybrid retrieval, knowledge graphs, and reranking to achieve optimization. Generation and task-output evaluations were reported in 27 studies, whereas retrieval evaluation, safety and reliability evaluations, and implementation or outcome evaluations were less frequently reported. Only 4 studies were conducted in real-world clinical settings. Overall, RAG demonstrated potential to improve the accuracy and reliability of LLM-generated outputs in specific nursing tasks; however, most studies validated only in simu

title: Lead Optimization in Drug Discovery: Integrating Advanced Computational Approaches for Enhanced Drug Design.
desc: [Current computer-aided drug design] The process of drug discovery is complex, lengthy, and expensive; it can take more than a decade to succeed and demands significant investments of financial resources. Despite these efforts, drug candidates still experience high failure rates during clinical trials. Computeraided Drug Design (CADD) has emerged as a powerful tool to overcome these obstacles in pharmaceutical research. CADD is used for drug development, such as target identification, lead discovery, optimisation, ADMET, and drug repurposing. CADD reduces the time and cost of drug discovery. Computational chemistry, bioinformatics, and structural biology are incorporated to predict drug-target interactions. The two major methodologies used to identify and optimise potential drug candidates are Structure-Based Drug Design (SBDD) and Ligand-Based Drug Design (LBDD). Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, Quantitative Structure- Activity Relationship (QSAR) modelling, pharmacophore modelling, and virtual screening are the techniques that allow efficient prediction of binding affinity, molecular behaviour, and biological activity. The recent advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has also enhanced CADD tools by screening large datasets, predicting pharmacokinetic properties, and designing new molecules. These developments have boosted the efficiency, accuracy, and success rate of drug discovery. (CADD) reduces time costs, as do the physical and technological capabilities of the field of computational technologies. The integration of AI continues to grow, and CADD is bound to assume a more crucial role in designing safer and more efficient therapeutic agents in the future. In this review, we will discuss the general concepts of CADD, the methodologies of CADD, and CADD in drug discovery.

title: Explainable AI identifies recombination and chromatin environment as key predictors of subgenome evolution in maize and Brassica.
desc: [Science advances] Polyploidy, or whole genome duplication, reshapes genomes through biased gene loss and regulatory rewiring, yet the drivers of biased fractionation among subgenomes remain unclear. Using maize and Brassica rapa as model allopolyploids, we compiled 60 genomic and epigenomic features in maize and 45 in B. rapa and constructed supervised machine learning models to classify genes by subgenome identity. In both species, eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) approaches identified recombination rate as the most influential and highly interconnected feature despite nonsignificant mean differences between subgenome groups. Chromosome location, transposon density, and chromatin-associated features, including the proximity of accessible chromatin regions to genes and active histone marks such as H3K9ac and H3K27ac, consistently ranked among the top contributors to subgenome classification. XAI-derived covariation and interaction networks further revealed recombination rate as the central node connecting significant features. Together, these results highlight recombination and chromatin environment as major predictors of subgenome divergence in polyploid genomes.

title: Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development (LATENT): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
desc: [Circulation] Electrocardiographic analysis aided by artificial intelligence (AI) may identify atrial electrical vulnerability during sinus rhythm. The objective of this study was to determine whether AI-enabled ECG (AI-ECG) is effective for detecting atrial fibrillation (AF), atrial flutter (AFl), or prespecified pre-AF atrial findings in a randomized trial. In this single-center, open-label trial, 14 665 adults 40 to 85 years of age without previous AF/AFl were randomized to an AI-ECG-guided strategy or usual care. Participants randomized to AI-ECG who were then identified by AI as having a high-risk sinus-rhythm ECG in the preceding year were offered Holter monitoring for ≤7 days. Each monitored high-risk intervention participant was paired with an age- and sex-matched control selected before control ECGs underwent AI analysis. Matched controls received identical monitoring to reduce ascertainment bias. Reporting cardiologists were blinded to AI results and randomized assignment. The primary outcome was a composite of newly detected AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings within 90 days. Pre-AF atrial findings comprised frequent premature atrial complexes, short runs of premature atrial complexes, or nonsustained AF/AFl. Among 7337 intervention and 7328 control participants, 84 (1.1%) and 78 (1.1%), respectively, were classified as high risk. Of the 84 high-risk intervention participants, 48 (57.1%) underwent monitoring, as did 48 matched controls. The primary outcome occurred in 54 intervention participants (0.74%) versus 35 control participants (0.48%; odds ratio, 1.54 [95% CI, 1.01-2.37]; P=0.046). Hypothetical reclassification of 1 intervention event to a nonevent changed the primary analysis P value to 0.057. The intervention effect on detection of the primary composite outcome differed by baseline AI-ECG risk (Pinteraction<0.001): 32.1% versus 2.6% among high-risk participants and 0.4% versus 0.5% among low-risk participants. AF/AFl detection (0.3% versus 0.2%) and antiarrhythmic therapy initiation at 180 days (2.3% versus 2.4%) did not differ significantly between the intervention and control groups. Participant-reported monitoring-related adverse events, including skin reactions and discomfort, occurred in 22.9% of monitored intervention participants versus 18.8% of matched controls. AI-ECG-guided monitoring resulted in a modest increase in the detection of new AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings. However, these findings were fragile statistically and sensitive to

title: SRNR: Deep learning-based MRI super-resolution using noisy high-resolution reference data.
desc: [Imaging neuroscience (Cambridge, Mass.)] Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) techniques offer a powerful tool to enhance the spatial resolution of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) without increasing scan time. However, most supervised SR methods rely on high-resolution, high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) reference data for training, which are difficult to acquire in many clinical settings, such as in time-constrained pediatric imaging. Inspired by the Noise2Noise principle, we propose SRNR, a new training paradigm that enables supervised SR using noisy high-resolution images as references. SRNR was systematically evaluated on both pediatric and adult simulated data across different noise levels of the reference data. SRNR generated super-resolved image volumes with high similarity to the high-resolution references (PSNR: 32.5-35.2 dB) and improved downstream image analysis performance, including tissue segmentation (white matter Dice coefficient: 0.951-0.960) and cortical surface reconstruction (cortical thickness absolute difference: 0.200-0.255 mm). Furthermore, SRNR was shown to be effective on clinically acquired pediatric brain MRI data, achieving improvements consistent with those observed in the simulated experiments. These results demonstrate that SRNR substantially reduces reliance on clean, high-SNR training data and enables effective SR under clinically realistic acquisition constraints, thereby improving the feasibility of deploying deep learning-based SR in pediatric MRI and related applications.

title: Evaluating the effectiveness of digital and intelligent technology-driven rehabilitation training following radical prostatectomy: A scoping review.
desc: [Geriatric nursing (New York, N.Y.)] The rapid growth of smart healthcare has integrated digital and intelligent interventions into care models. However, the impact of technology-driven rehabilitation on recovery after radical prostatectomy remains unclear, especially from the perspectives of patients and healthcare providers. This scoping review investigates the effects of these interventions on patients and examines how digital and intelligent technologies are incorporated into rehabilitation plans. A total of eight databases, searched from inception to January 20, 2025. Based on an a-priori protocol the JBI methodology for scoping reviews was used and the review reported against the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews. A total of 43 effective indicators were reported in the 12 included studies, with the number of effective indicators ranging from 1 to 11 in individual studies, with the most frequently occurring outcome indicators being physical activity behavior, degree of incontinence, and quality of life. As advances in digital health continue to evolve, future research should be committed to combining postoperative assessment and rehabilitation training through digital and intelligent means to deepen the understanding of enhanced recovery after surgery in digital health, thereby further improving the ability of nurses to use Digital health technology and services to support care.

title: Tissue-resident memory T cells: central regulators of chronicity and relapse in autoimmune diseases-from mechanistic insights to precision interventions.
desc: [Immunologic research] Tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM), a subset of memory T cells that persist long-term within peripheral tissues without recirculating, play a dual role in adaptive immunity. They serve as the frontline defense against pathogen reinfection, yet accumulating evidence implicates TRM cells as pivotal effectors driving chronicity, tissue-specific damage, and clinical relapse in various autoimmune diseases. This review systematically examines the central role of TRM cells in autoimmunity by dissecting the molecular mechanisms underlying their development, maintenance, and activation. We highlight how specific cytokine networks, alongside metabolic programs and sustain their pathogenic potential. Emphasis is placed on the heterogeneous functions of TRM cells in diseases such as psoriasis/psoriatic arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus and primary Sjögren's syndrome. Furthermore, we analyze the dysregulation of tissue immune checkpoints through interactions between TRM and regulatory T cells (Treg), which disrupt immune homeostasis. Finally, we critically evaluate current therapeutic strategies targeting TRM cells and propose future precision intervention approaches leveraging immune metabolic reprogramming, nanotechnology, and artificial intelligence to improve disease management and prevent relapse.

title: Integrated deep learning reconstruction combining phase correction, denoising, and super-resolution for prostate diffusion-weighted imaging.
desc: [Magnetic resonance imaging] To evaluate integrated deep learning reconstruction (Integrated DLR), which combines phase correction, denoising, and super-resolution, for prostate diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) by comparing it with compressed sensing (CS) and deep learning-based denoising reconstruction (Denoising DLR). This single-center, retrospective study included 47 patients scanned on a single-vendor 3-T system. Three DWI datasets were reconstructed from identical raw data using CS, Denoising DLR, and Integrated DLR. Two radiologists rated overall image quality, noise, artifact, and prostate delineation. Apparent signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) was assessed in all patients. In 21 patients with pathologically confirmed prostate cancer, we assessed lesion conspicuity, lesion localization/anatomical relationship, Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) version 2.1 DWI scores, apparent lesion contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Comparisons were performed using Friedman tests followed by Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Scores for overall image quality, noise, and prostate delineation were highest with Integrated DLR, followed by Denoising DLR and CS, for both readers (all p < 0.001); apparent SNR showed the same pattern (p < 0.001). Artifact scores did not differ among methods. Lesion conspicuity differed among methods for Reader 2 (p = 0.044) but not for Reader 1 (p = 0.199), whereas Integrated DLR yielded the highest lesion localization/anatomical relationship scores for both readers (both p < 0.001). Integrated DLR also yielded the highest apparent CNR and lesion ADC (both p < 0.001), while PI-RADS DWI scores were unchanged. Integrated DLR improved prostate DWI image quality and lesion visibility compared with CS and Denoising DLR, potentially facilitating visual assessment of prostate DWI.

title: Agentic AI in transforming agriculture: a review.
desc: [NPJ sustainable agriculture] Artificial intelligence-based agents are emerging as a transformative paradigm for agriculture, enabling autonomous perception, reasoning, decision-making, and coordinated action across complex data and operational environments. These systems could improve productivity, resilience, resource efficiency, and food security, while raising challenges related to robustness, interoperability, data governance, trust, equity, and regulation. This Review examines the rise of these systems in agriculture and outlines research priorities for their development and deployment.

title: RCIRNet: Rotator Cuff Injury Recognition Using Wearable IMU Signals With Cross-Attention.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
desc: [IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society] Rotator cuff injury (RCI) is a common cause of shoulder dysfunction, often accompanied by pain, restricted mobility, and reduced quality of life. Conventional imaging-based diagnostic approaches are effective for structural assessment but are often costly, time-consuming, and difficult to apply in large-scale screening or repeated follow-up. In this study, we propose the RCI recognition network (RCIRNet), a lightweight deep learning model for automated RCI recognition using upper-limb kinematic data collected from wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs). RCIRNet extracts temporal motion features with one-dimensional convolutional layers and introduces a channel-sequence cross-attention (CSCA) module to emphasize informative sensor channels and discriminative movement phases. Multi-segment acceleration signals from the upper thoracic spine, upper arm, and forearm during shoulder abduction are used to distinguish RCI from non-RCI conditions, including adhesive capsulitis and shoulders without dysfunction. Model performance is evaluated on an independent test set using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RCIRNet achieves an accuracy of 88.8%, an F1-score of 88.9%, and an AUC of 0.932, outperforming traditional machine-learning models as well as BiLSTM and Transformer Encoder baselines. These results suggest that IMU-based deep learning with channel-sequence attention provides a promising auxiliary tool for low-cost and non-invasive RCI screening.

title: Towards Reliable Measurement of Cerebellar Morphology: A Comparative Assessment of Segmentation Pipelines.
desc: [Cerebellum (London, England)] Characterizing cerebellar morphology is fundamental for accurately mapping its structure and function across individuals, yet remains challenging due to its densely foliated architecture. Although multiple automated segmentation pipelines exist, the measurement reproducibility of these tools has not been comprehensively benchmarked. We conducted a systematic assessment of reliability for cerebellar morphology estimates using four commonly used pipelines: one classic parcellation method (CERES), two deep-learning methods (ACAPULCO, DeepCERES), and one voxel-based morphometry toolbox (SUIT). Leveraging the HNU dataset, which provides MRI scans for ten timepoints per individual over a month, we evaluated the test-retest reliability for each of the four pipelines using ReX, an integrative tool for quantifying and optimizing measurement reliability and individual differences. We quantified intra- and inter-individual variability, as well as the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC), for each pipeline at both global and region-of-interest levels. We used two pools of data: a common dataset of 12 subjects x 5 sessions to benchmark all the pipelines, and method-specific datasets including pools of subjects with 5 valid sessions for each pipeline to assess the generalizability of our findings. Overall, all pipelines yielded highly reliable segmentation volumes (ICC > 0.87). DeepCERES demonstrated the most consistent performance across all metrics and subject pools, while SUIT achieved the highest ICC on the common dataset but showed decreased reliability when evaluated on a larger subject pool. Importantly, our analysis highlighted substantial heterogeneity in reliability across lobules for each method. Lobule X consistently showed reduced reliability whereas lobules I-V, VI, Crus I, IX, and VIIIB were reliably estimated across all pipelines. While all pipelines demonstrated strong reliability, DeepCERES showed the most robust and consistent performance overall. Substantial lobule-specific variability and method-dependent failure rates underscore the need for reliability-aware pipeline selection to optimize cerebellar morphology estimation in research.

title: Rethinking neural network reparameterized full waveform inversion: A Hessian perspective.
source: PubMed · Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
desc: [Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society] By seamlessly integrating deep neural networks (DNNs) into the traditional full waveform inversion (FWI) framework, the neural-network-reparameterized FWI (RFWI) naturally introduces implicit regularization, thereby mitigating key challenges in practical applications-such as sensitivity to initial models and susceptibility to local minima. While a variety of advanced RFWI methods have been proposed to enhance inversion performance, profound insights remain lacking in two key questions: (1) How does the DNN improve the robustness of RFWI, (2) How to further improve the performance of RFWI. In response to the first question, the Hessian spectrum is introduced as an analytical tool to reveal the difference in optimization characteristics between RFWI and traditional FWI. Our findings demonstrate that the superior robustness arises from the persistent constraints imposed by DNN on the inversion process, guiding a long-lasting tendency towards the eigenvectors associated with large eigenvalues, which correspond to stable directions dominated by low-frequency information. For the second question, we propose two improvement techniques based on the inherent optimization characteristics of RFWI, targeting convergence or robustness, both of which have the potential to generalize to other RFWI implementations. Focusing on convergence improvement in ideal scenarios, we propose the Adam+L-BFGS hybrid optimizer, which accelerates high-frequency fitting while avoiding local minima. Regarding robustness improvement in challenging scenarios, we propose a Hessian trace-based regularization technique that promotes flatter optimization trajectories, thereby mitigating the overfitting of noise. The experimental results support the effectiveness of our proposed improvement techniques.

title: From Identification to Integration: Twenty-Five Years of Proteomics and Metabolomics through the Pages of the Journal of Proteome Research.
desc: [Journal of proteome research] As the American Chemical Society marks its 150th anniversary, it is a fitting moment to reflect on how a young analytical discipline, proteomics, matured into a central pillar of the chemical and biological sciences and how the Journal of Proteome Research (JPR) chronicled and guided that transformation. Founded at the dawn of shotgun proteomics, JPR has published pivotal advances in separation, ionization, computational interpretation, quantitative strategies, and biological applications. In this Perspective, we trace that arc from the first near-complete eukaryotic proteomes through the quantitative and post-translational era, the computational turn, and the current high-throughput, integrative, and artificial-intelligence-assisted phase. Along the way, we highlight how the same infrastructure enabled mass spectrometry-based metabolomics, yielding an integrated framework for molecular phenotyping.
